brief: Design an interface for a "Dream Residue Collector" that helps lucid dreamers capture and categorize the fleeting sensory fragments that remain just after waking—those ephemeral images, sounds, and fe

dominant_strengths: Conceptually rich gesture-as-input metaphor for ephemeral dream content—maps emotion to motion in a poetic, intent-aligned way
Soft italic labels and dim navy field create a genuinely liminal, pre-waking emotional register
Floating fragment bubbles with varied scale suggest memory drift rather than rigid grid taxonomy
dominant_weaknesses: Three legend glyphs (red cone, blue trapezoid, green ring) feel like mismatched primitives—different rendering languages collide and break craft
Gesture legend is buried as plain text top-left while glyphs sit bottom; instructional system is spatially disjointed and unscannable
No visible captured-residue state, timestamp, or progress beyond a thin gradient bar—behavioral loop is unclear
fix_priorities: Unify the three category icons into one rendering system (all volumetric, all line, or all gesture-trace)
Co-locate gesture instruction with its category icon so legend reads as one coherent key
Introduce a visible residue archive or capture confirmation to close the interaction loop
Tighten typographic hierarchy—differentiate fragment labels from category labels with weight or size
rationale.norman_balance: Strong reflective and visceral pull from the dreamy palette and metaphor, but behavioral clarity lags—how to actually capture a fragment is ambiguous.
rationale.intent_fit: Conceptually it nails the brief's poetic ambition, but executional inconsistency in the icon system undermines the categorization mechanic it promises.
